content_voiceover: This diagram catalogs the abnormal red cell morphologies tied to membrane alterations, and each shape reflects a specific biophysical defect. Target cells reflect an increased surface area to volume ratio, either an absolute increase in phospholipid and cholesterol as in obstructive liver disease, or a relative increase from reduced cell volume, as in iron deficiency, thalassemia, hemoglobin E, or hemoglobin C. Acanthocytes show cholesterol accumulation in the outer leaflet, seen in liver disease, or sphingomyelin accumulation, seen in abetalipoproteinemia. Echinocytes reflect outer bilayer expansion relative to the inner surface, seen in uremia, pyruvate kinase deficiency, or as an artifact. Spherocytes arise from spectrin, ankyrin, or band 3 deficiency causing membrane instability, lipid loss, and a falling MCV, that is hereditary spherocytosis, or from reticuloendothelial removal of antibody coated membrane, that is autoimmune hemolysis. Elliptocytes come from altered horizontal spectrin dimer interactions, the classic mechanism in common HE. Stomatocytes reflect expansion of the inner bilayer surface, seen with vinca alkaloids, alcoholism, or cation permeability disorders. And poikilocytes or fragments reflect severely impaired horizontal protein interactions, as in hemolytic HE or hereditary pyropoikilocytosis, or mechanical causes like microangiopathy or intravascular prosthesis.
keypoints: Target cells: ↑SA:volume — liver disease, Fe deficiency, thalassemia, Hgb E/C
Echinocytes: uremia, PK deficiency, or artifact
keypoint_voiceover: Match the shape to the mechanism. Target cells mean increased surface to volume ratio, think liver disease or iron deficiency and thalassemia. Spherocytes come from spectrin, ankyrin, or band 3 loss, either hereditary spherocytosis or autoimmune hemolysis stripping the membrane. Elliptocytes reflect impaired horizontal spectrin interactions, the hallmark of hereditary elliptocytosis. Acanthocytes point to liver disease or abetalipoproteinemia, and echinocytes to uremia or PK deficiency.
